page.name: Service and incident alerts
page.h1: Send the outage notice from a path that is still up
page.metaTitle: Service and incident alerts that get through
page.metaDescription: Maintenance notices and incident updates sent to affected accounts, with failover so the alert about an outage is not the casualty.
page.lede: An incident alert arrives when something is already wrong — the worst possible moment to discover your send path is down too. Keep more than one connected account on that channel, and the notice about the outage is not its first casualty.

sections.h: What belongs in an incident update
bullets: What is affected, in plain terms
What the recipient should do, if anything
When the next update will come
A link to the live status page
p: Send an update when the state changes, not on a fixed cadence that produces messages with nothing new in them. A silence that was promised is better than a message that says nothing.

sections.h: Two connected accounts, so the notice still leaves
p: Incident traffic should not depend on a single provider account — the day you need it is the day you cannot afford a second failure. On the SMS channel, traffic can route to another connected account when one stops accepting traffic, and receipts show what actually left.
bullets: Automatic failover between connected SMS accounts
Per-number pacing so an affected-account send does not stall
Receipt status recorded so “we told them” is provable

sections.h: Scope the list, or lose the audience
p: Sending an incident alert to every address you hold is how a service message becomes noise. Scope the recipient list to genuinely affected accounts — the platform sends to the list you give it, so the accuracy of that list is on your side.

faq.q: Can alerts be sent on WhatsApp as well as SMS?
faq.a: You can connect the accounts you hold on each channel. Automatic failover between accounts is implemented for the SMS channel.

faq.q: Do we need a second provider to make this work?
faq.a: Failover needs somewhere to fail over to, which means more than one connected account on that channel.
A service or incident notice to an affected account is transactional, so it is not filtered by promotional suppression.
